args.platform.note: CLI -p/--platform (type=int, no default => None when omitted). null=omitted (None, falsy); 0=explicit zero (falsy); 1=smallest positive int (truthy).

encoding: Python truthiness test `if args.platform:` on an int symbol. bool(int) is (x != 0); None is also falsy. Encoded in z3 as Int('platform') constrained to the seeded explicit-int set {0,1} with pred = (platform != 0). Mirrors ExpressionEvaluator unary-truthy op-surface over an int-valued symbol. The None case is covered by Python semantics (bool(None)=False) and folded into the FALSE side.
notes: Pure truthiness branch: `if args.platform:` taken (TRUE) iff args.platform is a nonzero int; falsy when 0 or omitted (None). z3 proves both sides sat over the seeded domain (TRUE: platform=1; FALSE: platform=0); Python semantics confirm None and 0 are falsy, 1 is truthy. No isinstance/nodeType/os/filesystem/gpu probes -- driven entirely by public CLI input -p/--platform, so classified fully-static. Downstream: argParser.add_argument('-p','--platform', type=int) means the value is an int or None; '-p 1' takes the TRUE branch (sets rv['Platform']=1, prints '# Command-line override: Platform'); omitting it (None) or '-p 0' takes the FALSE branch. No PURE helper with a nontrivial postcondition exists for CrossHair: the predicate is a single bare truthiness test (def platform_override(p): return bool(p)) with no relational contract to falsify, so no CrossHair run is reported (absence of a counterexample would not be a proof anyway). The z3 proof above is the load-bearing witness.
